status_summary: As of 2026-10-22 the IRA half of this objective is largely enacted through reconciliation while the IIJA half has not been repealed: per the amended U.S. Code, Public Law 119-21 (signed 2025-07-04) ends the home energy efficiency and residential clean energy credits (26 U.S.C. 25C and 25D) after 2025-12-31 (sections 70505 and 70506) and the clean vehicle credit (30D) for vehicles acquired after 2025-09-30 (section 70502), limits the clean hydrogen credit (45V) to facilities whose construction begins before 2028-01-01 (section 70511), denies the wind and solar credits (45Y and 48E) to facilities placed in service after 2027-12-31 whose construction begins after 2026-07-04 (sections 70512 and 70513), ends the advanced manufacturing credit (45X) for wind components after 2027 and metallurgical coal after 2029 with critical minerals phased out after 2033 (section 70514), extends the clean fuel credit (45Z) through 2029 (section 70521) and repeals the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund (section 60002), and, per CRS, it rescinded unobligated balances of several IRA programs, including DOE loan programs, while appropriating 1 billion dollars for section 1706 loan guarantee costs available through FY2028. Executive Order 14154 (2025-01-20) paused IRA and IIJA disbursements, and DOE announced on 2025-10-01 the termination of 321 awards supporting 223 projects, estimated at about 7.56 billion dollars in savings. Courts have since ordered reinstatement of 27.6 million dollars in commitments (January 2026) and vacated 11 grant cancellations worth 82.1 million dollars (2026-06-11), and 13 states sued over hydrogen hub cancellations (2026-02-18). The FY2026 Energy and Water act (Division B of Public Law 119-74, signed 2026-01-23) gave the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations no funding and, per CRS, transferred about 5.165 billion dollars of unobligated balances to other DOE programs and 3.1 billion dollars from IIJA programs for small modular reactors, rather than cancelling the 15.247 billion dollars of IIJA advance appropriations the Administration had asked to cancel.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14154 orders agencies to pause disbursement of IRA and IIJA funds pending review, with release subject to review and approval by OMB and the economic policy adviser.

Public Law 119-21 is signed. Per the U.S. Code text as amended: the residential clean energy credit ends for expenditures after 2025-12-31 (section 70506), the clean vehicle credit for vehicles acquired after 2025-09-30 (section 70502), and the clean hydrogen credit requires construction to begin before 2028-01-01 (section 70511); wind and solar facilities placed in service after 2027-12-31 lose the section 45Y credit (section 70512); the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund statute is repealed (section 60002). The law's table of contents also lists rescissions of other IRA funds (Sec. 50402 and further rescissions in Title VI) and Energy Dominance Financing (Sec. 50403), which were not read in the enrolled text.

timeline.event: IRS Notice 2025-42 on beginning-of-construction rules for wind and solar takes effect for construction starting on or after this date; it states the credits end for facilities placed in service after 2027-12-31 unless construction began before 2026-07-05 (the notice's issuance date is not shown on the page).

DOE announces it has terminated 321 financial awards supporting 223 projects, with estimated savings of about 7.56 billion dollars, issued by OCED, EERE, GDO, MESC, ARPA-E and Fossil Energy; DOE says a case-by-case financial review found the projects did not adequately serve energy needs or return enough value, notes that 26 percent of the terminated awards were made between Election Day and Inauguration Day, and gives recipients 30 days to appeal. S&P Global reports the two largest awards, 2.2 billion dollars, were for West Coast hydrogen hubs.

The FY2026 Energy and Water appropriations act, Division B of Public Law 119-74 (H.R. 6938), is signed. Per CRS Report R48599 it provides no funding for the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations and, in section 311, transfers about 5.165 billion dollars of unobligated balances from EERE, civil nuclear credit and carbon capture accounts to other DOE programs and 3.1 billion dollars from IIJA programs for up to two small modular reactors, where the Administration had asked to cancel 15.247 billion dollars of IIJA advance appropriations.

California, Washington and other states sue DOE in the Northern District of California over the October 2025 cancellations of hydrogen hub and other awards, arguing the cuts violate separation of powers and that a May 2025 DOE review memorandum is a pretext.

A federal judge in the District of Columbia vacates DOE's cancellation of 11 EERE grants worth 82.1 million dollars (date inferred from an article published 2026-06-12); a January 2026 ruling in a similar case had ordered DOE to reinstate 27.6 million dollars in commitments on equal protection grounds.

title: Repeal IIJA and IRA energy programs and rescind unspent funds
uncertainties: On 2026-10-22 the amended Code pages hosted by law.cornell.edu were re-read for 26 U.S.C. 25C, 25D, 30D, 45X, 45Y, 45Z and 48E and 42 U.S.C. 7434 (45V was read in an earlier review and not re-read), and their notes cite Public Law 119-21 (2025-07-04) for the credit end dates, the 45Z extension and the repeal of the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund; the 25C end date no longer rests on a law-firm alert. The enrolled text of Public Law 119-21 itself was still not read (the govinfo.gov copy ends in the first title, at section 10507). The IRA loan rescissions and the 1 billion dollar section 1706 appropriation rest on CRS Report R48599 as copied on everycrsreport.com, read through a summary of the page; it names the IRA programs rescinded but not the sections of the 2025 law (it prints the section 1706 IRA citation as 40144), gives no dollar figure for the rescinded balances, does not mention Title VI or the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund, and does not say that the 1 billion dollars goes to the renamed Office of Energy Dominance Financing; the Energy Dominance Financing section number (50403) and the loan rescission section number (50402) come from the law's table of contents. An external retrieval of the enrolled text describes further Title VI rescissions without dollar amounts and reports no rescission of IIJA funds in Title VI; none of this was independently opened, and its section range was not verified. Facilities that began construction by 2026-07-04 keep the earlier wind and solar rules, and IRS Notice 2025-42 addresses beginning of construction. The FY2026 Energy and Water figures (no OCED funding, about 5.165 billion dollars in section 311 transfers, 3.1 billion dollars from IIJA programs, and the 15.247 billion dollar cancellation request) rest on the same CRS report because the Division B text on govinfo.gov could not be read; the earlier Holland & Knight figure of about 5.164 billion dollars of unobligated IIJA funds was written before signing, and CRS does not label all of the 5.165 billion dollars as IIJA funds. CRS dates the DOE award terminations to 2025-10-02, while the DOE release used here is dated 2025-10-01; DOE's release was read through a page summary. The 13-state suit and the January 2026 outcome rest on S&P Global, and the 2026-06-11 ruling (Judge Mehta, D.D.C., per Utility Dive) has no caption or docket number and its date is inferred from an article published 2026-06-12. Utility Dive's description of the January outcome (a settlement versus an order) is inconsistent. Litigation over the January 2025 funding pause was not researched.
